name: Spin-Glass Quench Dynamics on D-Wave Annealer
description: Benchmark of real-time spin-glass quench dynamics on D-Wave superconducting annealers against state-of-the-art classical tensor-network and neural-network simulators. The collaboration showed that for 2D, 3D and infinite-dimensional spin glasses the annealer produces samples in close agreement with the Schrödinger equation while leading classical methods cannot match the accuracy within reasonable runtimes. The paper argues this is a regime where quantum simulation offers a genuine, application-framed advantage for dynamics questions relevant to condensed-matter physics.
significance: Shifts the D-Wave story from combinatorial optimization to physics-simulation advantage, a domain where classical tensor-network methods had previously been considered competitive.

news.title: Beyond-classical computation in quantum simulation
news.excerpt: Superconducting quantum annealing processors can rapidly generate samples in close agreement with solutions of the Schrödinger equation for spin-glass quench dynamics. Several leading approximate methods based on tensor networks and neural networks cannot achieve the same accuracy as the quantum annealer within a reasonable time frame.
